title: EEG-Based Prediction of Music Enjoyment Using Deep Learning with Explainable Temporal Analysis
abstract: arXiv:2610.20795v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Understanding why listeners enjoy music is difficult because the experience is subjective and changes as a piece unfolds. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers a non-invasive way to study neural responses during listening, yet earlier work has mostly treated music emotion as a categorical label or relied on black-box models. We formulate enjoyment prediction as a regression problem on the public MUSIN-G dataset, which contains 128-channel EEG from 20 listeners together with song-level enjoyment ratings. Six deep learning models were compared under a participant-wise protocol, in which 15 listeners were used for training and validation and 5 were held out for testing. DeepConvNet, CNN-LSTM and GNN-CNN reached the lowest mean absolute error (0.97 to 0.99 on the 1 to 5 scale), while the temporal convolutional network (TCN) had the highest Pearson correlation with the ratings (r = 0.21). translated_abstract: 理解听众为什么喜欢音乐很困难，因为这种体验是主观的，并且会随着乐曲的展开而变化。脑电图（EEG）提供了一种非侵入性的方式来研究聆听过程中的神经反应，然而早期的研究大多将音乐情感视为分类标签，或依赖于黑盒模型。我们将音乐享受度预测形式化为公开MUSIN-G数据集上的一个回归问题，该数据集包含20名听众的128通道脑电数据以及歌曲层面的享受度评分。研究在参与者级别的协议下比较了六种深度学习模型，其中15名听众用于训练和验证，5名听众被保留用于测试。DeepConvNet、CNN-LSTM和GNN-CNN达到了最低的平均绝对误差（在1到5的量表上为0.97至0.99），而时间卷积网络（TCN）与评分的皮尔逊相关性最高（r = 0.21）。基于梯度和基于遮挡的解释方法，通过平均……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文将音乐享受预测从传统的分类任务转化为回归问题，在公开EEG数据集上比较了六种深度学习模型，并结合可解释性技术进行时间维度的神经反应分析。
